newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stock rises for second day in row.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stock rises for second day in row.

text.p: Jordanian stocks rose for the second consecutive day on Tuesday with continued investor confidence in government steps to advance free-market reforms in the wake of bread riots, dealers said.

The official Amman Financial Market 60-share index rose 0.28 percent to 141.70 points from 141.31 points on Monday, the second day it rose above the key 140-point psychological barrier for the first time since the riots broke out a week ago.
The market first fell below 140 points at the end of June, sliding to levels not reached since 1993 with lack of cash liquidity and minimal institutional support dampening investor sentiment.
A total of 631,059 shares changed hands on Tuesday in a healthy 823,221 dinar turnover in the cash-squeezed market.
Blue-chip Arab Bank, a major component of the official 60 share index, that led the market pickup on Monday with a 7.50 dinar rise shed 1.50 dinars.

The market rose on Monday a sharp 1.46 percent with investors positively reacting to a government pledge to encourage private sector investment and specifically a new companies law that would cancel a 15 percent tax levied on companies' capital increases.
Arab Bank, seen to be a main beneficiary of the new companies law, was target of continued buying for the second day with over 133,360 dinars in turnover.
The Pearl Investable Index -- an independent index of the 45 best-performing shares from the official market -- firmed 0.36 percent to 80.73 points. It was 15.48 percent down on last year.

Tuesday's second consecutive rise this week represented an increase of almost two percent in the index over the last week, as the market recovered from unrest fuelled by the government's decision this month to almost double prices of bread in line with IMF-agreed economic reforms.
The riots were the worst in Jordan since 1989.
In banks, the leading sector: blue-chip Arab Bank shed 1.50 dinars to 227.00 dinars while Jordan Islamic Bank rose 20 fils to 3.60 fils on a turnover of 15,328 dinars.
In industrials, the leading sector, Jordan Cement Factories rose 20 fils to 3.360 dinars and Livestock and Poultry was unchanged at 530 fils.
In services, Jordan Electric Power shed 10 fils to 1.530 dinars and National Portfolio was unchanged at 1.180 dinars.

Industrials dominated on Tuesday, with a 515,229 dinar turnover and an index rise of 0.81 percent, banks had a 182,866 dinar turnover and an index drop of 0.14 percent while services had a low 123,968 dinar turnover and an index rise of 0.42 percent.
A total of 1206,617 shares worth 80,393 dinars changed hands in weak trade in the parallel market.
